key_insight: Supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding produces denser, harder Cr3C2–NiCr coatings than conventional APS, but this mainly boosts wear resistance rather than erosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical coating design, axial-fed HV-APS is a strong upgrade path over radial APS when the goal is lower porosity and improved tribological performance.
method: APS: conventional atmospheric plasma spraying with radial powder injection (A60 torch)
HV-APS: supersonic axial powder feeding (Axial III torch)
Compared microstructure, phase composition, erosion, and ball-on-disc wear on Cr3C2–NiCr coatings
evidence_signal: Compared with APS, HV-APS reduced porosity from 11.99% to 6.16%, increased microhardness from 897 to 1141 HV0.2, and lowered wear volume from 3.90 to 2.85 mm3, while erosion rates stayed nearly unchanged (0.20 vs 0.19 mg/g).
watch_item: The improved density and hardness did not translate into better erosion resistance at a 90° impact angle, so application conditions must be checked before selecting the process.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
